newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes softer ahead of Cetes auction.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes softer ahead of Cetes auction.

text.p: The peso closed softer across the board on Tuesday amid demand from local and foreign players covering short dollar positions ahead of an expected drop in primary interest rates, traders said.
"The market discounted a forthcoming fall in interest rates, so dealers covered dollar shorts," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both ended 1.1 centavos weaker at 7.7620/7.7650 and 7.7600/7.7630 per dollar, respectively.
"The peso slipped suddenly, it felt very odd, and volume was heavy," another trader said.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 0.9 of a centavo weaker at 7.7510/7.7540 per dollar.
Traders said they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to fall by up to 70 basis points from last week's assignment rate of 19.46 percent.
Banco de Mexico is due to announce the results of this week's primary auction of government securities at 1830 local time.
Other dealers attributed the peso's late slide against the dollar to demand from corporations to meet month-end obligations payable in dollars.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.7550/7.7700 per dollar on Wednesday for 48-hour contracts.
